definitions.full: H669. Ephrayim אֶפְרַ֫יִם proper name, masculine Ephraim ( Gen 41:52 connected with הִפְרָה , Hiph`il of פרה , compare פרא Hiph`il Hosea 13:15 ). 1 2nd son of Joseph Gen 41:52 ; 46:20 ; reckoned among sons of Jacob, blessed by him, and given preference over Manasseh 48:1 , 5 , 13 , 14 , 17 (twice in verse) (compare 48:19 ) 48:20 ; 48:20 ; 50:23 ; Num 1:10 ; 1Chr 7:20 , 22 . 2 אֶפְרַיִם בְּנֵי (= descendants, tribe of east) Num 1:32 ; 2:18 (twice in verse); 2:24 ; 7:48 ; 10:22 ; 26:35 , 37 ; Josh 16:5 , 9 (boundaries of territory), 17:8 ; 1Chr 9:3 ; 12:31 ; 27:10 , 14 , 20 ; 2Chr 28:12 ; less often א ׳מַטֵּה Num 1:33 ; 13:8 ; Josh 21:5 ; 1Chr 6:51 ; בְנֵיאֿ ׳מַטֵּה Num 34:24 ; Josh 16:8 ; compare 14:4 ; א ׳שֵׁבֶט Psa 78:67 (|| יוֺסֵף אֹהֶל ); א ׳בֵּית Judg 10:9 ; also ׳א alone, tribe Ephraim Num 26:28 ; Deut 33:17 ; Josh 16:10 + often; א ׳אֶרֶין וּמְנַשֶּׁה 17:17 compare Judg 12:15 ; 2Chr 30:10 especially 3 הַראֶֿפְרַיִם the mountain-country of Ephraim , a ridge stretching from north to south through territory assigned to Ephraim, with fruitful land on both slopes, especially the western (compare Di Josh 16:1 ) 17:15 ; 19:50 ; 20:7 ; Judg 2:9 ; 3:27 ; 4:5 26t. 4 by Hosea & Isaiah (rarely later) אֶפְרַיִם = kingdom of northern Israel (from Ephraim as largest & strongest tribe in it) Hosea 4:17 ; 5:3 (twice in verse); 5:5 (|| יִשְׂרָאֵל ) 5:11 ; 5:12 30t. Hosea; Isa 7:2 , 5 , 8 , 9 , 17 9 t. Isaiah; also Jer 7:15 ; 31:9 , 18 , 20 ; Ezek 37:16 (strike out Co) 37:19 ; Psa 78:9 ; 2Chr 25:7 , 10 ; compare 30:1 ; Psa 60:9 = 108:9 ; א ׳עָרֵי 2Chr 17:2 ; compare 34:6 ; א ׳שְׂדֵה Obadiah 19; hence ׳א alone in local sense 31:1 ; also Hosea 5:9 , where feminine (& perhaps Isa 7:2 ). 5 אֶפְרַיִם יִעַר 2Sam 18:6 , east of Jordan; ᵐ5 L Klo read מַחֲנַיִם יער compare 17:24 , 27 . 6 name of a city near Baal-hazor 2Sam 13:23 (= Ἐφραϊμ John 11:54 & 1 Macc 11:34? Klo compare ᵐ5 L Γοφραιμ & עפרון , Qr עֶפְרַיִן 2Chr 13:9 ; so previously Bö Th Ke compare Dr). 7 אֶפְרַיִם שַׁעַר a chief gate of Jerusalem 2Kin 14:13 ; 2Chr 25:23 ; Neh 8:16 ; 12:39 ; perhaps at northwest angle, near Holy Sepulchre, compare Schick-Guthe ZPV 1885 . אֶפְרָת see אפרתה . below

Jehoshaphat lived at Jerusalem; and he went out again among the people from Beersheba to the hill country of Ephraim, and brought them back to Yahweh, the God of their fathers.
A man of God came to him, saying, “O king, don’t let the army of Israel go with you, for Yahweh is not with Israel, with all the children of Ephraim.
Then Amaziah separated them, the army that had come to him out of Ephraim, to go home again. Therefore their anger was greatly kindled against Judah, and they returned home in fierce anger.

Joash king of Israel took Amaziah king of Judah, the son of Joash the son of Jehoahaz, at Beth Shemesh, and brought him to Jerusalem, and broke down the wall of Jerusalem from the gate of Ephraim to the corner gate, four hundred cubits.‡ A cubit is the length from the tip of the middle finger to the elbow on a man’s arm, or about 18 inches or 46 centimeters, so 400 cubits is about 200 yards or 184 meters.
Zichri, a mighty man of Ephraim, killed Maaseiah the king’s son, Azrikam the ruler of the house, and Elkanah who was next to the king.
